title: Milestone set
description: Contract for docs/internal/PRODUCT/MILESTONES.yml, the milestone SSOT. GitHub milestones are a projection of this file, never the other way round. Enforced by scripts/check-milestones.mjs (INV-146, #2480).

milestones.description: Live and upcoming milestones only. The migration is forward-only: closed pre-MS work stays in MILESTONES.md, which is an archive. Exit-criteria evidence is never reconstructed after the fact to satisfy the gate.

epics.description: The epic index. An epic lives as a GitHub issue; this is the committed side of it, because the gate is offline by contract (INV-13) and cannot ask GitHub what it says. Sharing the milestone SSOT is deliberate: an epic that targets no milestone, and a milestone claiming an epic that does not exist, are the same defect seen from two sides, and only a reader holding both can see either.

id.description: Registered in docs/internal/SYSTEM/ID-REGISTRY.md. NOT the bare `M` prefix, which is methodology measures M1-M16.

goal.description: GSN Goal. A milestone states a claim about the world, not a list of tasks — the tasks are `members`.

claim.description: What is true once this milestone is verified.

strategy.description: How the exit criteria are argued to establish the claim. GSN Strategy.

exit_criteria.description: GSN Solutions. What would have to be shown for the claim to hold.

evidence_ref.description: Resolvable pointer to the artifact that discharges this criterion: a gate name, a path under .arbiter/evidence/, or an INV id. Required by the gate before `status: done` — its absence is what makes `done` fail-closed.

members.description: What rolls up into this milestone. An epic that targets no milestone is the defect the shared gate exists to surface.

label.description: GitHub label used to reconcile the projection.

depends_on.description: Must form a DAG across the set; the gate rejects a cycle.

horizon.description: Now/Next/Later. Granularity decays with distance — see the allOf rules below.

due.description: Required for `now`, optional for `next`, forbidden for `later`. A date on a `later` milestone is false precision, so the schema refuses it rather than trusting a convention.

status.description: `done` requires every exit criterion to carry an evidence_ref (gate-enforced, fail-closed). `verified` additionally requires those refs to resolve.

then.description: A milestone claimed to be in flight has a date and a size, or it is not really `now`.

epic.description: A decomposable unit of work targeting exactly one milestone.

issue.description: The GitHub issue this epic IS. One issue may back at most one epic, and may not also appear in a milestone's members.issues — the same work claimed twice is a claim the join cannot reconcile.

targets.description: Exactly one milestone. The targeted milestone must list this epic in members.epics; the gate checks both directions, because a one-sided link is how an epic silently detaches from the plan.

status.description: `abandoned` is not a euphemism for `drained` and the ladder does not treat it as one: work can stop because it shipped or because it was dropped, and a roadmap that cannot say which has lost the only distinction that matters when reading it later. Both are terminal and both demand an evidence_ref. This rung exists because the first three epics recorded here were all closed — one completed, two not-planned — while the file called them open (#2480, wave 8).

evidence_ref.description: Required by the gate for a terminal status (`drained`, `abandoned`) — the same fail-closed discipline a milestone's exit criteria carry, for the same reason: status is a claim, not evidence. A `github:` ref is accepted unresolved because this gate never reaches the network.
